description: Single, wages + interest: Virginia standard deduction and one exemption
working: Form 760: line 1 federal AGI 66,500; no additions or subtractions; line 9 = 66,500. Federal standard deduction was taken, so Virginia standard deduction 8,750 (line 11). Line 12 exemptions 1 x 930 = 930. Line 15 Virginia taxable income = 66,500 - 8,750 - 930 = 56,820. Tax: 2% x 3,000 = 60; 3% x 2,000 = 60; 5% x 12,000 = 600; 5.75% x (56,820 - 17,000) = 5.75% x 39,820 = 2,289.65. Total 3,009.65. Federal: 66,500 - 16,100 = 50,400; tax = 1,240 + 12% x 38,000 = 5,800.

description: Joint, both 65+, itemizing federally: uncapped property tax, 10% medical floor, $800 age exemptions; age deduction is zero at this income
working: Form 760: federal AGI 180,000. Itemized on the federal return, so Virginia itemizes (Schedule A, state income tax removed, no SALT cap, medical floor 10%): medical 20,000 - 10% x 180,000 = 2,000; real estate tax 12,000; mortgage interest 14,000; total 28,000 (> 17,500 standard). Exemptions: 2 x 930 + 2 x 800 (65+) = 3,460. Age deduction: adjusted income 180,000 exceeds 75,000 by more than 2 x 12,000, so 0. Taxable income = 180,000 - 28,000 - 3,460 = 148,540. Tax = 720 (on first 17,000) + 5.75% x 131,540 = 720 + 7,563.55 = 8,283.55. Federal: itemized = medical 20,000 - 7.5% x 180,000 = 6,500 + SALT (12,000 + 8,283.55 state tax = 20,283.55, under the 40,400 cap) + mortgage 14,000 = 40,784 (rounded) > 35,500 standard (32,200 + 2 x 1,650); senior deduction 2 x (6,000 - 6% x 30,000) = 8,400; TI = 180,000 - 40,784 - 8,400 = 130,816; ordinary 105,816 -> 11,600 + 22% x 5,016 = 12,703.52; 25,000 of gains/dividends at 15% = 3,750; income tax 16,453.52 -> 16,454.
